jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.description:
Role Description
In this role, you’ll be the customer's voice as you collaborate with Engineering, Product, Experience Research, Data Science, and business partners to build compelling products. You will solve problems with cross functional partners in collaborative teams, that enable designers to do their best work. As part of a product-driven and design-led company, you'll play a key role in a team of Product Designers owning core product development from inception to iteration and post-launch reflection. If you’re looking for scope, influence and the opportunity to do high-quality work in your next role, this is it.
This role is based in our Vancouver office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements.
About the design team
We design the future of teamwork. Asana has a bold, ambitious mission: help humanity thrive by enabling the world’s teams to work together effortlessly. Our design team is at the heart of that mission.
Asana Design is an inclusive and collaborative community. We’re a diverse group of designers from different backgrounds (product, brand and content design, design operations, producers, motion design, film, copywriting). We are a team that loves combining research, data insights, and peer feedback into a human-centered design process to produce designs that are core to the power of our applications. We partner with people across Asana to create our product, shape our brand, and drive greater impact through design. We use design to solve challenges and create experiences that customers love. We also take the time to get weird and have fun along the way.
We believe every designer should have the opportunity to grow and learn by utilizing their strengths and nurturing their interests.
Learn more about our team
- Asana Design

About you
- 3+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong thinking, craft, and iteration across onboarding, growth, or AI-powered product experiences.
- Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making.
- Strong prototyping skills and a maker mindset. You use prototypes regularly to explore ideas, test concepts, and drive collaboration.
- Excited by highly collaborative product development and comfortable working closely with PMs and engineers throughout ideation and iteration.
- Comfortable navigating ambiguity, moving quickly, and balancing incremental optimization work with longer-term product exploration.
- Exceptional visual and interaction design craft, with the ability to create polished, intuitive, and high-quality product experiences across every stage of the user journey.
What you’ll achieve
- Lead the design of end-to-end experiences for Asana products and features, with an emphasis on features for billing owners.
- Collaborate with cross-functional partners to identify customer problems, establish vision, set strategy, build and ship solutions.
- Champion product excellence. Elevate the quality bar for our experience and shape our payment design system.
- Work across the organization to ship experiences that are cohesive with the broader Asana product experience, ensuring your design scales.
- Facilitate and role model human-centered problem solving. Foster co-creation across the organization.
- Learn new methods to solve deeply complex problems in the service of inventing new ways to deliver our customer benefits: flow, efficiency, engagement, and retention.
- Help shape a product that is intuitive and elegant, which speaks from a unified voice.

Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit.

jobs.title: Product Security Engineer
jobs.description:
At Asana, security is foundational to our mission of helping humanity thrive by enabling the world's teams to work together effortlessly. Our security team protects Asana's employees, users, and customers by proactively addressing threats and fostering a culture of security throughout our product and operations.
We're looking for a Product Security Engineer to join our Product Security team in Warsaw. You'll be a foundational member of the security presence in a key engineering hub, partnering directly with product and infrastructure teams to ensure we design and ship secure software. You will be instrumental in scaling our security practices by building secure-by-default frameworks, eliminating entire classes of vulnerabilities, and championing a security-first mindset across our web, mobile, and AI-powered product surfaces.
This role is based in our Warsaw office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do, and your recruiter can share more about the in-office requirements.
We offer a Contract of Employment (UoP) for our employees in Poland.
What you'll achieve
- Partner with product and engineering teams across the full software development lifecycle to ensure security is designed and built into Asana's products and platform.
- Conduct security architecture reviews, threat modeling, and code reviews for new features and services.
- Develop, implement, and maintain secure-by-default frameworks and libraries that empower engineering teams to build secure systems easily.
- Build and maintain automated security tooling (static and dynamic analysis rules, custom SAST/DAST checks, and automated red-teaming) to scale security coverage without scaling headcount.
- Identify and address AI-specific security risks such as prompt injection, insecure tool permissions, and abuse-resistant design in Asana's AI and agentic features.
- Triage, investigate, and drive remediation of vulnerabilities from our bug bounty program, internal testing, and automated security tooling.
- Influence engineering initiatives by conducting design and roadmap reviews, effectively communicating security constraints, and assisting teams in making informed trade-offs.
- Investigate product security incidents as a subject matter expert, using logs and monitoring tools to contain, analyze, and drive resolution.
- Evaluate and improve software supply chain security, including dependency management, SCA tooling, and third-party risk in the development pipeline.
- Develop and deliver training to educate engineers on secure coding best practices and emerging threats.
- Stay informed of industry trends, emerging threats, and best practices to ensure that Asana's security posture remains robust.
- Collaborate with teammates and stakeholders to develop both short-term and long-term strategies for risk management.
About you
- 5+ years of experience in application security, product security, or software engineering with a security focus.
- Strong software engineering background with experience in languages like Python, Javascript/Typescript or Scala.
- Deep working knowledge of the OWASP Top 10 and common web application vulnerabilities such as XSS, CSRF, SSRF, and SQL injection.
- Familiarity with AI/ML security concepts, including LLM-specific risks such as prompt injection and agentic attack surfaces.
- Experience with security tools for static/dynamic analysis (SAST/DAST), software composition analysis (SCA), and vulnerability management.
- Experience performing security design reviews and threat modeling for complex applications.
- Excellent communication skills for collaborating effectively with both technical and non-technical partners.
- A pragmatic and collaborative mindset, with a passion for building defenses against real-world attacks and enabling other engineers to do their best, most secure work.

Our tech stack includes: AWS, Kubernetes (EKS), MySQL (RDS), OpenSearch, DynamoDB, Redis, Terraform, Datadog, TypeScript, Scala, Go, and Python.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Threat Response
jobs.description:
Our Security team keeps Asana's employees, users, and customers safe, by proactively addressing threats and fostering a culture of security throughout our product and operations.
We are looking for a savvy Security Engineer to join our Blue Team. You will be a foundational member of the security presence in our Warsaw innovation hub, partnering directly with IT, infrastructure, and product teams to ensure we have robust detection and response capabilities. Detection and response here leans on engineering practice. We are investing in automation and detection-as-code to cut down on manual triage, and we are looking for someone comfortable writing and reviewing code as part of that work.
This role is based in our Vancouver office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. - Lead detection, analysis, and response across our cloud and SaaS environments, identity providers, endpoints, and the software supply chain, ensuring timely and effective remediation of security incidents.
- Investigate and remediate security incidents across cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP/Azure), identity providers (e.g., Okta), and SaaS environments.
- Investigate and contain software supply chain and CI/CD incidents, from unauthorized changes in build environments to suspect third-party dependencies (e.g., npm, PyPI).
- Help build and maintain our detection-as-code infrastructure (e.g., Panther), SOAR automation, and response playbooks, treating detection logic as tested, version-controlled production code.
- Utilize and optimize security tools such as Panther for SIEM, CrowdStrike for endpoint detection and response, and other security platforms.
- Conduct proactive threat hunting and operationalize threat intelligence across cloud, endpoint, and identity telemetry to catch threats beyond standard SIEM alerting.
- Conduct forensic analysis during security incidents to understand the scope and impact of incidents.
- Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate security best practices into development processes and provide guidance on secure configurations.
- Develop and deliver training to educate engineers on security operations and incident response best practices.
About you:
- 8+ years of experience in threat detection, security operations, or incident response, including investigating incidents across cloud platforms, identity providers, and SaaS applications, with practical knowledge of audit logging and IAM.
- Proficient in Python (Bash, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript is a plus) for security scripting and automation, with hands-on experience across REST APIs, Git workflows, and PR-based code reviews.
- Hands-on experience investigating software supply chain threats, with fluency in auditing modern developer ecosystems (e.g., npm, PyPI), build logs, and CI/CD pipelines.
- Familiarity with "Detection as Code" methodologies, including test-driven detection logic and rule management through CI/CD pipelines.
- Strong experience with SIEM platforms (e.g., Panther, Splunk, Elastic Security) for log analysis, alert correlation, and dashboard creation.
- Deep working knowledge of endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools (e.g., CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) with specialized expertise in macOS endpoint security, telemetry, and threat detection capabilities.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Query and Access Control
jobs.description:
We're looking for a staff software engineer to work on how data is queried and who is allowed to see it. Every read in Asana passes through this layer: it resolves what a user is asking for and enforces, on every object, whether that user is permitted to see it. You will help us keep those guarantees correct and fast as our largest customers grow their domains, their permission structures get more intricate, and AI agents become a significant new class of caller.
The Query and Access Control team owns the query execution path over the Work Graph and the permissioning model that governs it. As a staff engineer on the team, you will take on our hardest technical problems and drive the work that spans several teams, bringing depth to the design decisions that shape this layer for years. We work closely with other teams in the core infrastructure area to build and retain customer trust in Asana as the platform for their critical workflows.
This role is based in our Reykjavik office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. What you'll achieve
- Design and implement a query layer over the Work Graph that stays correct and performant as customer domains and permission structures grow
- Evolve our access control model so that permission checks remain sound, auditable, and fast on every read path
- Define how new classes of caller, including AI agents acting on a user's behalf, are authorized, without weakening the guarantees customers depend on
- Drive large, multi-quarter projects that cut across team boundaries, from design and implementation through deployment and iteration
- Build alignment on the design with engineers and leaders in other teams before the code is written, and keep that alignment as the work lands
- Share what you know through design review, code review, and mentorship
- Partner with infrastructure teams across Asana to define how user data in the Work Graph is accessed
- Support framework and product engineers to build new product functionality at scale, quickly

- You have driven large technical initiatives spanning multiple teams, and perhaps organizations, from early design to adoption

- You are skilled at communicating technical concepts and constraints to cross-functional partners in product

- Working knowledge of at least one detection or query language (Sigma, KQL, SPL, YARA-L, EQL, or Panther), or strong SQL or Python skills and the drive to learn one quickly.

- Hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, ideally including identity and access logs.
- Have used SIEM, EDR, or SOAR tools in any size of environment.
- Write clearly in runbooks, design docs, and incident notes, and can own well-scoped projects end to end.

- Have led purple team, blue team, or adversary emulation exercises that improved detections or telemetry.
- Experience running SIEM, EDR, or SOAR platforms at large scale.
- Experience building or maintaining detection-as-code workflows (version control, CI, and tests for detections).
- Experience applying LLMs or agent-style tooling to security workflows.
- Experience securing AI-enabled systems or endpoint tooling.

- Have hands-on experience operating endpoint management and detection tooling across macOS and enterprise environments.
- Write production-quality scripts and automation in Python or Bash, and have shipped Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for security configuration.
- Are familiar with SaaS security risks (OAuth governance, audit logging, SSPM) and the realities of integrating a long tail of vendors.
- Have working knowledge of at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure) at the security configuration level.

You’ll build the systems that let any knowledge worker leverage fast, scalable databases without having to become a DBA.
You’ll be a hands-on technical leader, helping set the architectural direction and roadmap as we take a new product from early alpha to general availability. You’ll work directly with early customers to shape foundational technical and product decisions. Then, together, we’ll work on scaling as adoption and workloads grow.
This is a backend-leaning role with work spanning the stack. You might build the systems that provision and manage a fleet of customer Postgres instances, design how user-defined schemas evolve safely, or make complex queries execute efficiently. You’ll also follow those systems into the product: improving how a table loads, how users understand a slow operation, or how an agent safely works with their data.
You’ll help shape the architecture and the product together. Some problems call for a better abstraction, others for a better default, and others for rethinking what we ask the user to do in the first place. You’ll work with teammates and customers to find those answers, ship practical solutions, and evolve them as usage grows.
Our stack includes Postgres, Go, TypeScript, Node.js, and React.
About the Team:
The people who understand a business best aren’t always the people who can build its software. A support lead knows how tickets should be triaged. An operations manager knows how inventory should move. But turning that knowledge into a reliable system often means finding an engineer, provisioning a database, and building an application.
We’re building database infrastructure for everyone else. We want everyday knowledge workers to bring their data into Notion, connect it, and build workflows around it. And do so with the power of a real database (Postgres!) and the approachability of a tool they already know.
AI agents make that opportunity even bigger: helping people build and operate systems they couldn’t have created on their own.
For our team, this is much more than putting a friendly interface on Postgres. It means making hard database problems disappear from the user’s workflow without sacrificing correctness, performance, or flexibility. How do you let someone reshape a live database as easily as editing a document? Make the right indexes exist without asking someone to become a DBA? Let a weekend experiment grow into a company’s system of record without anyone having to rearchitect it?
What You'll Achieve:
- Take a new product from alpha to general availability. Work with early customers to understand what matters, iterate on feedback, and help shape what we ship.
- Make real customer workloads fast. Improve query execution, indexing, and client data loading so performance holds up as datasets grow and workflows become more demanding.
- Build systems businesses can trust with their data. Make schema changes, concurrent writes, permissions, and recovery reliable enough for customers to build essential workflows on top.
- Make powerful capabilities approachable. Turn database provisioning, migrations, and indexes into a reliable, easy-to-use product experience that gives people the power of a database without the burden of managing one.
- Build for the customers who come next. Automate database provisioning and fleet operations, strengthen observability, and evolve the architecture so we can serve many, many customers.
Skills You'll Need to Bring:
- Production relational database experience (e.g., Postgres or MySQL). You’ve made decisions about schemas and indexes, analyzed database performance, and debugged issues involving transactions, locking, or concurrency. Your experience goes beyond accessing a database through an ORM.
- Engineering experience and technical leadership. You bring 10+ years of experience building and operating production software, with a track record of setting technical direction and leading complex, cross-team initiatives from concept through delivery. You identify the most important problems to solve, turn ambiguous goals into a technical strategy, and align engineers and partner teams around a practical plan. You stay hands-on while helping others make better decisions through design reviews, mentorship, and clear technical guidance.
- Strong backend engineering fundamentals. You’ve built services that need to remain correct under concurrency and failure. You can reason about retries, partial failures, consistency, and the trade-offs involved in reliable reads and writes.
- A systematic approach to performance. You use query plans, traces, profiles, and experiments to find bottlenecks and verify improvements. You’re willing to follow a problem across storage, services, and client code rather than stopping at a team boundary.
- Product judgment. You’re interested in who will use what you build, not just how it works. You can turn a customer’s problem into a technical approach and recognize when a better default or simpler workflow would solve it more effectively.
- Willingness to work across the stack. You bring backend depth, but you’re comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and working in client code when that’s what delivering a good experience requires.
- Fluency with AI-assisted engineering. You use AI to accelerate exploration, implementation, and testing while taking responsibility for understanding and validating the result.

- Experience managing fleets of databases or building database platforms, including provisioning, upgrades, backups, and recovery.
- Deep Postgres expertise, such as advanced query optimization, performance tuning, or workload isolation for large datasets and high-concurrency workloads.
- Experience building query layers, sync engines, change-data-capture pipelines, permission systems, or other reusable data abstractions.

- Lead the team’s hardest initiatives from idea to operation. Ensure complex work has strong technical ownership, de-risk architectures through prototypes, break work into shippable milestones, and coordinate execution across engineers and teams.
- Make Notion’s data platform enterprise-ready. Guide the team toward durable foundations for external key management, data residency, access controls, lifecycle management, and governance without creating separate systems for every requirement.
- Raise reliability, simplicity, and cost efficiency. Identify systemic risks and architectural gaps, establish clear service ownership, and lead migrations that make Kafka, Debezium, S3/Iceberg, Spark, EMR, Athena, and related systems easier to operate at scale.

You’ll ship high-signal detections, improve the platform that powers them, participate in incident response, and help shape how detection and response engineering scales at Notion.
You’ll work closely with Engineering, Corporate Security, and Infrastructure, with broad latitude to identify gaps, prioritize investments, and build what’s needed next.
We view detection and response as a software engineering discipline: detections are code, platforms are products, and measurement matters
What You'll Achieve
- Build and tune high-signal detections across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS environments, with review and mentorship from senior teammates as you ramp up.
- Contribute to the detection platform, including rule lifecycle management, tuning, measurement, and rollout safety.
- Build tooling and automation that speed up triage, enrichment, investigation, and detection authoring, including LLM-based workflows where useful.
- Turn threat intelligence and adversary TTPs into detections, telemetry requirements, and response improvements.
- Take part in investigations, incident response, and postmortems, and help turn what we learn into lasting fixes.
- Help define and track metrics such as coverage, MTTD, and alert quality.
- Join a shared on-call rotation for incident response.

- We're hiring across a range of experience levels. If you have some of these skills but not all, we'd still like to hear from you.
- 3+ years of experience in detection engineering, security operations, incident response, threat hunting, or a closely related security or software engineering role.
- Have written or tuned detections that run in production, and care about signal quality and cutting noise.
- Working knowledge of at least one detection or query language (Sigma, KQL, SPL, YARA-L, EQL, or Panther), or strong SQL or Python skills and the drive to learn one quickly.
- An understanding of how attackers operate (for example, MITRE ATT&CK), and the ability to use it to decide what to detect.
- Hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, ideally including identity and access logs.
- Have used SIEM, EDR, or SOAR tools in any size of environment.
- Write clearly in runbooks, design docs, and incident notes, and can own well-scoped projects end to end.
Nice to Have
- Have led purple team, blue team, or adversary emulation exercises that improved detections or telemetry.
- Experience running SIEM, EDR, or SOAR platforms at large scale.
- Experience building or maintaining detection-as-code workflows (version control, CI, and tests for detections).
- Experience applying LLMs or agent-style tooling to security workflows.
- Experience securing AI-enabled systems or endpoint tooling.
- Kubernetes or container detection experience.
- Background in threat intelligence, malware analysis, or digital forensics.

- Experience at a high-growth startup or AI company.

jobs.description:
Who We Are
Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.
This internship will take place from May 24 - August 13 or June 14 - Sept 3 (based on your summer schedule) and you will need to be able to work out of our NY office during this time.

- Learn how a production iOS platform works: Get exposure to shared frameworks, build systems, release quality, and our shared Rust layer.

jobs.title: AI Engineer, Internal Tools
jobs.description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!
Figma employees are among the most AI-active in the industry, and our Internal AI team, part of FTS (our Business Technology org), helps turn that energy into meaningful impact by making it easier for every Figmate, from Sales and Support to Finance, People, and Legal, to safely adopt AI and use it to improve how they work.
We’re a small, high-leverage team organized around three pillars: Platform & Tooling, Infrastructure & Hosting, and Applied AI Builds, and this role is a key member of the Applied AI Builds pillar.
As an AI Engineer, Internal Tools, you’ll work directly with teams across Figma to identify high-value AI opportunities and take them to production, moving from understanding a business workflow, to rapidly prototyping an approach, to evaluating it and integrating it with the systems and data needed to make it useful in the real world.
This isn’t a role focused only on building AI demos: you’ll own solutions through production, help determine where AI adds value and where traditional rules-based software is the right choice, and shape how agents can safely take actions across enterprise systems. As common patterns emerge, you’ll partner with our Platform & Tooling and Infrastructure teams to build reusable capabilities that make future AI builds faster and safer.
This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.
What you’ll do at Figma:
- Partner directly with teams across GTM, Finance, People, Legal, Support, and other business functions to understand workflows and identify high-value opportunities for AI
- Design, build, and productionize AI agents, assistants, and workflow automations that solve real business problems using LLMs, tool calling, RAG, structured outputs, agent frameworks, MCP, APIs, and enterprise data
- Integrate AI applications with enterprise systems and data sources across GTM, Finance, People, Support, and internal APIs
- Build evaluations and feedback loops to measure accuracy, reliability, and business impact before and after AI solutions reach production
- Design deterministic guardrails, human-in-the-loop controls, and approval patterns for workflows where AI systems take business-critical actions
- Build production-ready systems with strong observability, failure handling, security, authentication, authorization, and auditability
- Identify reusable patterns across individual AI projects and build them out as shared components and capabilities in partnership with our Internal AI platform teams
- Help define how Figma approaches Applied AI engineering and scales AI adoption across the company
We’d love to hear from you if you have:
- 5+ years of software engineering experience building production applications, integrations, backend systems, or AI-powered products
- Hands-on experience building applications with LLMs, agents, retrieval-augmented generation, function calling, schema-constrained outputs, or evaluation frameworks
- Experience taking an AI application or workflow beyond a prototype and operating it in a production environment
- Strong API, integration, and system design fundamentals, with experience connecting applications across multiple systems and data sources and strong engineering judgment about when to apply AI and when a rules-based approach is the right choice, and experience designing reliable production systems with appropriate observability, failure handling, authentication, authorization, and security controls
- Experience working directly with non-engineering stakeholders to understand ambiguous business problems and translate them into technical solutions and ability to move quickly from discovery to prototype while understanding what is required to safely and reliably productionize a solution
While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:
- A background building internal AI applications or working in an Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineering, or AI Solutions Engineering role
- Experience with MCP, agent orchestration frameworks, and enterprise tool-calling patterns
- Knowledge of AWS Bedrock, AgentCore, OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar AI platforms
- Experience integrating enterprise systems such as Salesforce, Zendesk, Workday, NetSuite, Greenhouse, or Slack
- Knowledge of with AI evaluations, observability, prompt/version management, and human-in-the-loop systems
- Experience implementing enterprise identity and access patterns such as Okta, SSO, OAuth, and secure service-to-service authentication, within Security, Privacy, SOX/ITGC, or other enterprise governance requirements

- Experience using a scripting language such as Python or R, as well as proficiency with SQL, for analysis, modeling, or work with complex or large-scale datasets through research, internships, or applied projects
- Ability to explain technical concepts clearly and connect analysis to decisions, recommendations, or product/business impact
- A curious, rigorous, and self-starting mindset, with the ability to thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and translate research into real-world impact

- Prior industry or applied research experience with experimental design, causal inference, forecasting, product measurement, user research, or applied machine learning to influence product, business, platform, or stakeholder decisions

- Experience or interest in AI product measurement, LLM analytics/evaluation, recommendation systems, search, personalization, or evaluating AI-powered features

jobs.title: Solutions Architect
jobs.description:
About the Team
The Innovation Architect sits within Miro's Professional Services organization, specifically inside the MOST (Miro Optimization Services & Training) program. MOST is Miro's subscription-based PS offering for enterprise customers. Each customer gets 240 hours per year to work with Miro experts on designing, implementing, and scaling how their teams collaborate. Innovation Architects work alongside Customer Success Managers, Technical Architects, and Engagement Managers to deliver structured, outcomes-driven engagements across some of Miro's most complex accounts.
About the Role
Enterprise customers have the hours. What they often don't have is someone who can translate where they want to go into a concrete, sequenced plan for getting there inside Miro. That's the gap this role fills.
The Innovation Architect is the strategic and architectural layer of a MOST engagement. They run discovery, diagnose how teams actually work today, design the governance and collaboration infrastructure to support where the customer is heading, and build the roadmap for how 240 hours get used across the year. They also own AI workflow advisory, helping customers move from ad hoc Miro usage to intelligent, repeatable collaboration systems.
This role is open because the program is growing and the complexity of enterprise accounts has outpaced what CSMs and Technical Architects can absorb on top of their core scope. The right candidate has a consulting background, is fluent in collaboration platforms, and is comfortable running live discovery with a skeptical CTO and a frustrated Product Lead at the same time. They own delivery quality from day one.
What you’ll do
- Own the solution roadmap for a portfolio of MOST accounts: run structured discovery, map the customer's operating model, and design a sequenced 240-hour plan tied directly to their business outcomes
- Architect end-to-end Miro implementations covering workspace governance, access models, naming conventions, and lifecycle management for organizations operating at scale
- Lead AI workflow advisory as a core workstream: diagnose collaboration inefficiencies and build intelligent, automated solutions using Miro's AI capabilities and adjacent platform integrations
- Facilitate executive and cross-functional working sessions including Agile planning, design thinking, strategy, and innovation workshops
- Drive adoption through change management: stakeholder alignment, communication planning, phased rollouts, and hands-on coaching on Miro best practices
- Track progress against defined outcomes across the full subscription lifecycle, surface risks early, and adjust the plan as priorities shift
- Contribute reusable delivery assets (templates, frameworks, playbooks) that raise the consistency floor across PS and reduce time-to-value for future engagements
What you’ll need
- 6+ years in consulting, change management, Agile transformation, or professional services supporting enterprise organizations
- Experience leading structured discovery with VP-level and above stakeholders and turning ambiguous findings into a clear, prioritized plan
- Working knowledge of collaboration governance: workspace architecture, access models, naming conventions, and lifecycle management at enterprise scale
- Fluency in Miro or a comparable collaboration platform (Figma, Lucid, Confluence, JIRA)
- Hands-on experience designing AI-powered workflow optimization: automation, prompt-based workflows, or AI-assisted tooling in an enterprise environment
- Able to simplify complex governance and architecture topics for non-technical audiences without losing the thread
- Comfortable working across IT, Product, Design, Strategy, and PMO simultaneously, often with conflicting stakeholder priorities
- Strong technical fluency: familiarity with APIs, integrations and enterprise IT ecosystems.
What's in it for you
We want you to feel supported, connected, and ready to grow. Our global benefits package generally includes equity, a wellbeing benefit, a WFH equipment allowance, and an annual Learning & Development stipend. Join a diverse team where you can do your best work. Full benefits may differ per location. If you would like to learn more about location-specific benefits, please refer to our Global Miro benefits board.
#LI-AN1

Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.
We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Optimize/Analyze to help develop and scale Webflow Optimize products.
You’ll design high-performance systems that adapt user experiences in real time, working with large-scale data processing and distributed computing to lift conversion and personalization at scale. Our team is fast-moving, data-driven, and experienced in personalization, ML infrastructure, and large-scale analytics.
The next chapter is ambitious. We’re serving some of the world’s largest enterprises and rethinking what an AI-native conversion platform can be. This is a cross-team technical role: you’ll work across a large, revenue-generating system, help decide what it needs to become, and partner directly with Engineering, Product, and Design to ship it.

- Permanent, full-time employee (this is not a contractor position)

- Deep hands on experience architecting an enterprise identity provider, with Okta strongly preferred
- Fluency in SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, and SCIM, including debugging at the token and assertion level
- Experience with identity governance, including RBAC design, HRIS driven lifecycle automation, and meeting audit requirements
- Strong grounding in Zero Trust and identity based attacks, including device trust and the security of non human identities
- Scripting ability (Python, JavaScript, or similar) and infrastructure as code experience, such as Terraform
- Clear communication with senior and executive audiences, including driving architecture decisions
- Nice to have: experience governing identities for AI tools and agents, and Okta certifications

- Design like an attacker, asking how every control could fail or be abused, and respect that one policy change can lock out the whole company
- Get results with Security, HR, and application owners through influence, not authority
- Care as much about adoption as correctness
- Bring order to an under managed environment without waiting for a perfect plan
- Use AI tools with good judgment
- Are comfortable as the lead identity expert, mentoring others and setting the standard
- Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.
We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure/SRE Engineer to improve the reliability and stability of the customer-facing production infrastructure behind Webflow’s Convert pillar.
Convert owns a suite of products that give marketing and growth teams the tools to experiment, personalize, and drive real revenue from their web presence, including Webflow Analyze, Optimize, AEO, and Campaigns. As tens of thousands of projects launch on Webflow each month, you’ll help keep the platform secure, scalable, and dependable for the people who rely on it.
Much of what Convert delivers depends on data: high-volume event ingestion, real-time and analytical data stores, and pipelines that turn visitor behavior into reporting, experiments, and personalization. You’ll own the reliability, performance, and cost of this data infrastructure, including streaming and batch pipelines and analytical databases. You’ll set SLOs, build observability, plan capacity, and make sure data stays fresh, accurate, and available as volume grows.
The next chapter is ambitious. We’re serving some of the world’s largest enterprises and rethinking what an AI-native conversion platform can be. You’ll work across a large, revenue-generating system, partner with the engineers who build on it, and help decide how it needs to evolve.
About the role:
- Location: Remote-first (USA and Argentina)
- Permanent
- Exempt
- United States (all figures cited below are in USD and pertain to workers in the United States)
- Zone A: $187,500 - 225,000
- Zone B: $176,700 - 212,000
- Zone C: $165,000 - 198,000
- Application Information:
- Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
- This posting is for a new position.
As a Senior Infrastructure/SRE Engineer on the Convert pillar, you'll:
- Own and evolve the cloud infrastructure behind the Convert products, including compute, serverless, networking, and cloud operations on AWS.
- Build and maintain our infrastructure-as-code foundation in Pulumi, and evolve the patterns and shared components other teams build on.
- Improve scalability and reliability of distributed, event-driven systems, including our Druid, MongoDB, and Airflow workloads, with a focus on low latency.
- Make observability the foundation of how we operate. Improve the dashboards, alerts, and SLOs for the systems you own so we catch issues before customers notice, and on-call pages are actionable instead of noisy.
- Lead projects from design through launch that move team and engineering org goals.
- Write and review maintainable, tested, performant code and automation, and raise the quality bar for the team.
- Build AI-powered automation, from policy-as-code and drift detection to LLM-assisted runbook generation, and use AI tools in your daily work.
- Help the team build reliable systems.
About you
Requirements:
- BA/BS degree or equivalent experience
- Business-level fluency to read, write and speak in English
You’ll thrive as a Senior Infrastructure/SRE Engineer if you:
- Have 5+ years owning and operating cloud infrastructure in a customer-facing environment with little tolerance for downtime. You come from infrastructure, SRE, or cloud engineering with a love of automation and code, or from software engineering with a deep interest in cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.
- Have deep hands-on experience with AWS and a clear view of what good cloud operations look like.
- Have used infrastructure as code (Pulumi or Terraform) and prefer changes made through code, not consoles.
- Have operated high-throughput, data-intensive distributed systems in production, such as Druid, MongoDB, or Airflow, and understand scalability, fault tolerance, consistency trade-offs, and performance tuning.
- Are fluent in Python or TypeScript/Node.js for automation and tooling, and can read and work in Java services.
- Treat observability as the basis of operations: you design SLOs, dashboards, and alerts so that issues surface before customers notice and pages are actionable.
- Handle incidents well, including on-call and blameless postmortems, and fix the root causes behind them instead of just closing tickets.
- Want to improve developer productivity, with CI/CD, tooling, and paved paths that let product engineers ship without owning infrastructure.
It would be a bonus if you had even one of the following:
- Experience with Apache Spark, Airflow, or TensorFlow.
- Familiarity with Kafka or other event streaming platforms.
- Experience building AI-assisted infrastructure tooling, including cost optimization loops, anomaly detection, or policy-as-code with LLM assistance.
- Experience contributing to multi-region architecture including data residency, regional failover, or latency-based routing.

jobs.title: Demo Software Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
About The Opportunity
As a Demo Software Engineer (f/m/d) you will be responsible for developing digital applications showcasing the use of Contentful within well-established categories and emerging areas. You will be the first to see new product features and play a critical role in bringing them to the market by building demos featured in product launches, analyst calls and annual customer conferences. In the off-season, you will help Contentful users get the most out of the product by developing how-to guides and tutorials, recording technical videos, and - occasionally - conducting in-person workshops.
This is a hands-on position that requires solid development skills and experience in shipping successful digital applications. You will be routinely asked to create things from scratch and craft delightful interaction loops, so creative thinking and good UX instincts are important for this role. Expect to be working on a wide range of tasks - frontend, backend, QA, devops - and a diverse set of projects spanning web, mobile, internal tooling, and AI. The demo team operates a modern technology stack and has a lot of say in deciding what tools and architectural patterns to use on the job.
While the core Demo team is small, we work with numerous stakeholders to deliver on our goals. We partner with Sales, Product, Engineering and Partnership teams to identify key business requirements and technical specifications for demo assets. We are experienced at augmenting our team with freelancers, agencies, and partners when tackling large-scale development projects. And we work closely with other marketing teams to drive product adoption through long-term educational programs and ad hoc campaigns.
What To Expect?
Be a part of an agile development team with a high impact across the organization:
- Support popular customer use cases and enable integrations with leading cloud providers, AI services and SaaS vendors
- Identify high-value technical problems and prototype quick solutions in the form of components, apps, integrations or full-fledged demo environments to address them.
- Master technical topics underpinning effective use of the Contentful platform, including content modeling, design systems, content orchestration, composable architectures, etc
- Develop expertise in using the customer-facing Contentful platform (e.g. APIs, CLI, webhooks, Forma36 design system, App framework, etc.) and internal systems (e.g. monitoring, deployment, AI-assisted development work)
- Effectively leverage devops infrastructure and AI tools to automate repetitive tasks, conduct effective QA, and support end-to-end workflows for internal users
- Prototype new integrations with our tech partners (among them OpenAI, Vercel, Algolia, Commercetools, Bynder, Ninetailed, Slack)
- Collaborate with Sales Engineering, Developer Relations, Solutions Architecture, and Product Marketing to create polished demo sites and apps
- Collaborate with Product Management, Engineering, and Design to implement new features in demo environments and provide effective product feedback
- Coach junior engineers and peers, act as a tech lead for cross-functional projects and projects delivered by external contractors
What You Need To Be Successful
- 6+ years of software development experience and/or systems engineering experience
- Strong technical experience with JavaScript, TypeScript and React
- Solid understanding of modern frontend frameworks (React/Vue/Svelte)
- Extensive experience working with APIs (including GraphQL API)
- Understanding of CI/CD workflows and devops best practices
- Ability to identify and prioritize high-impact problems and independently deliver solutions that provide reasonable effort/quality trade-offs
- Innate curiosity and ability to empathize with end users
- Good communication skills and ability to present complex technical concepts in an accessible way
- Proactive attitude and ability to master new topics quickly (there is a lot to learn on the job)
- Experience in full-stack development, working with AI, implementing design systems in production, launching mobile apps, and leading product development workshops is a plus
More details about our company benefits can be found at the following link: https://www.salesforcebenefits.com.
Contentful is now officially part of Salesforce.
Unleash Your Potential
When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
More details about company benefits can be found at the following link: https://www.salesforcebenefits.com
If you need reasonable accommodations at any point during the application or interview process, please let your Recruiter know.
Equal Opportunity Statement
Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination.
Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.
Please be aware of scammers who may fraudulently claim to be from Contentful. These types of fraud can occur through copycat websites, fake email addresses claiming to be from our company, or social media. We do not ask for your personal information, such as bank account numbers, identification numbers, etc., through social media or chat-based apps, nor do we request or send money to purchase business equipment. If you suspect fraud, please report it to your local authorities and contact us at security@contentful.com with any information you may have.

jobs.description:
About The Opportunity
Become part of the Contentful Personalization Team and help shape how leading businesses deliver personalized digital user experiences.
As a Senior Software Engineer, you will solve complex customer problems and deliver value through end-to-end personalization solutions. You will work across high-performance backend services, developer-facing frontend tools and SDKs, infrastructure, and observability to help customers deliver personalized content experiences in a performant, reliable, and developer-friendly way.
You will bring a proactive approach to problem-solving, a high sense of ownership, and a continuous improvement mindset. You will use modern AI tools, including agentic coding workflows, thoughtfully to improve how you explore, build, test, and maintain software. You will also contribute actively to the team's Agile ways of working, understanding how planning, refinement, delivery, reviews, retrospectives, and continuous improvement fit together.
What To Expect?
- Design, develop, and maintain high-performance backend services and APIs with a focus on reliability, scalability, and low latency.
- Deliver end-to-end solutions across backend services, React-based frontend experiences, and developer-facing SDKs, libraries, and tools.
- Implement complex CDN and edge-based caching solutions that allow users to retrieve personalized content in the most performant way.
- Solve technical challenges in creative ways, balancing the trade-off between performance and elegant software architecture.
- Continuously monitor and optimize system performance through benchmarking, while making sure systems are well instrumented for observability.
- Implement defensive coding practices and guarantee correctness and maintainable code through automated testing.
- Use AI-assisted and agentic coding tools responsibly to improve engineering workflows, while maintaining high standards for code quality, security, testing, and review.
- Participate actively in Agile ceremonies, including planning, refinement, reviews, and retrospectives, to help the team deliver customer value and continuously improve.
- Stay up to date with the latest technologies and constantly evaluate their potential use at Contentful.
What You Need To Be Successful?
- Proven experience building APIs and services that efficiently handle large volumes of traffic.
- Strong proficiency with server-side TypeScript and API protocol design.
- Experience delivering full-stack solutions, including React-based frontend experiences and SDKs, libraries, or tools for developers.
- Experience with serverless architectures, ideally edge compute environments such as Cloudflare Workers.
- Experience with CDN operations and caching strategies to optimize system performance.
- Hands-on experience with benchmarking, instrumenting code for observability, and performance optimization for large-scale systems.
- Expertise in defensive coding practices, ensuring system robustness and fault tolerance.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Applied AI Solutions
jobs.description:
Applications for this position will be accepted on an ongoing basis.
About The Opportunity
Contentful is looking for a Software Engineer to join our Applied AI product line with a primary focus on Marketplace. In this role, you will help build, maintain, and grow the systems, apps, and workflows that expand what customers can do with Contentful.
You will work across the Marketplace surface area and adjacent Applied AI tooling, helping us deliver high-impact apps, improve the contribution and review pipeline, and scale the ways internal and external developers build on top of Contentful. While Marketplace is the primary focus, this role should also be able to contribute across adjacent Applied AI areas like Extensibility and Developer Experience when priorities call for it.
This role is ideal for an engineer strong in front-end product work but not limited to it: someone comfortable moving between React surfaces, Node.js services, APIs, developer tooling, and production operations as needed. We are looking for a product-minded full-stack engineer who enjoys strong cross-functional collaboration and taking growing ownership of software through its full lifecycle in production.
We are also evolving how we build software. We increasingly use AI-assisted development workflows to accelerate delivery, reduce menial workload, and improve leverage across the software development lifecycle. We are looking for an engineer who is genuinely excited to experiment with these tools — not just adopt them passively, but bring strong engineering instincts to getting the most out of them.
This is a hybrid role, with office attendance in Denver expected 2 days per week (Tuesday, Thursday).
What To Expect?
- Design, build, and maintain Marketplace features, apps, and supporting services that improve the experience for both app builders and app installers.
- Contribute to the systems and tooling that help Contentful teams and partners bring new apps and integrations to market faster.
- Contribute across adjacent Applied AI problem spaces, including extensibility workflows, developer tooling, internal platform capabilities, and backend services that support developers building on Contentful.
- Improve contribution workflows, trust and safety checks, maintainability, and operational quality across Marketplace and Applied AI surfaces.
- Partner closely with product, design, and engineers across Applied AI to shape solutions that solve meaningful customer and business problems.
- Help generalize, polish, and productionize internally built apps and Applied AI contributions so they can be supported long-term by Marketplace Engineering.
- Own software in production, including debugging issues, improving observability, strengthening reliability, and participating in support and operational responsibilities.
- Use AI-assisted workflows across planning, implementation, debugging, and documentation where they create real leverage.
- Help the team improve how we use AI in engineering by sharing practices, refining workflows, and contributing to a healthy engineering culture around quality and speed.
What You Need To Be Successful
- Roughly 4-7 years of relevant software engineering experience
- Solid professional software engineering experience building and maintaining production systems.
- Strong experience with TypeScript and Node.js, plus solid experience building user-facing product surfaces in React or similar front-end frameworks.
- Clear strength in front-end engineering, paired with real comfort contributing to backend services, APIs, and developer-facing tooling rather than working exclusively in the UI layer.
- Experience designing and evolving APIs, integrations, and services used by other engineers, partners, or customers.
- Good judgment around reliability, maintainability, security, and technical tradeoffs in a product environment.
- Comfort working across the stack and across boundaries, from user experience to backend behavior to operational concerns.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, including experience working cross-functionally and asynchronously across teams and time zones.
- A product mindset and real empathy for developers, partners, and customers.
- Practical experience using AI tools to improve engineering productivity, with the ability to evaluate outputs critically and maintain a high quality bar.
Nice to Have
- Experience with developer platforms, SDKs, app frameworks, marketplaces, extensibility products, or integration ecosystems.
- Experience with AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Cloudflare, or related cloud infrastructure.
- Experience maintaining or contributing to public or shared developer tooling.
- Familiarity with AI-native product surfaces, agentic workflows, or systems that connect software to external tools and services.
What’s In It For You?
- Join an ambitious tech company reshaping the way people build digital experiences
- Comprehensive healthcare package covering 100% of monthly health premiums for employees and 85% of costs for your dependents.
- Fertility and family building benefits, including a lifetime reimbursable wallet to support your growing family.
- We value Work-Life balance and You Time! A generous amount of paid time off, including vacation days, sick days, compassion days for loss, education days, and volunteer days
- Company paid parental leave to care for and focus on your growing family
- Use your personal annual education budget to improve your skills and grow in your career
- Enjoy a full range of virtual and in-person events, including workshops, guest speakers, and fun team activities, supporting learning and networking exchange beyond the usual work duties
- An annual wellbeing stipend to care for your physical, financial, or emotional health

- Owning solutions, taking them all the way through delivery to adoption by engineering teams and customers;

- Experience designing and maintaining public libraries, SDKs or design systems, with a feel for API ergonomics and a track record of managing breaking changes

DataGrip is a core part of our ecosystem and revenue, but we currently lack a dedicated face to represent it to the outside world. We are looking for a Developer Advocate to take ownership of our public presence within developer communities and connect with our global users.
In this role, you will bridge the gap between our users and our product team. You will bring DataGrip to the center of the conversation by diving into online discussions, crafting advocacy content that provides value for years to come, and gathering the real-world feedback we need to build better tools. When we build and launch new database products, you will be involved in the product discussions from inception, leading the way.

- Build and sustain visibility across a massive, diverse landscape of database communities.
What you’ll bring
- A genuine enjoyment for talking to people and actively engaging with online developer communities all day.
- A natural curiosity for industry trends and evolving database technologies.
- An independent mindset comfortable with taking full ownership of public outreach and strategy.
- Strong communication skills that translate complex technical details into clear, engaging insights.

jobs.title: Ecosystem QA Lead
jobs.description:
You’re the kind of person who looks at a complex, deeply interconnected system and immediately wants to know how it functions and what would make it break. Focused on finding more than just bugs, you want to untangle dependencies and raise the bar for quality across the board. You're comfortable stepping up to take ownership and lead the charge when things get complicated.
About JetBrains
We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.
What you’ll do
DataGrip is our cross-platform IDE for databases, and its core functionality powers database tools across other JetBrains IDEs like IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and PhpStorm. Because of the large size of this ecosystem, which spans many database systems, environments, and integrations, keeping our quality bar high is a complex, strategic challenge. You’ll take ownership of quality across these shared components and release processes. You’ll work closely with developers, DevOps, and product teams to map out expected behaviors, investigate hard-to-reproduce issues, and improve how we build and test. Your work will directly influence the reliability of tools used by millions of developers every day, making sure changes in one area don't unexpectedly break another.
Day to day, you will:
- Lead QA activities, set priorities, and coordinate testing efforts across multiple teams and components.
- Investigate unclear, poorly reproducible, and cross-component issues to find the root cause.
- Analyze logs, test results, and user reports to spot broader quality patterns behind individual failures.
- Define test strategies and apply risk-based testing to manage release cycles safely.
- Work with developers and product teams to establish expected behavior when detailed specifications aren't available.
- Improve our QA processes and guide the team in making confident release decisions.
What you’ll bring
- A high degree of independence and technical curiosity.
- Comfort taking ownership of complex problems and driving them to resolution.
- The ability to see the big picture and understand how changes in one area affect the rest of the system.
- A proactive approach to improving processes rather than just following them.
- Strong analytical thinking, with the ability to turn scattered logs and user reports into clear insights.
- The communication skills to bring different teams together and coordinate testing efforts smoothly.
What you’ll need
- The proven ability to test complex, multi-component systems and navigate integration and end-to-end testing.
- Practical knowledge of relational databases and SQL.
- Experience leading QA activities and shaping test strategies for multiple products and release cycles.
- Familiarity with reading and debugging code (Java or Kotlin preferred) to troubleshoot deeply embedded issues.
- Hands-on experience writing or maintaining automated tests.
- The ability to navigate and troubleshoot CI/CD systems, test environments, and infrastructure (such as Docker, Kubernetes, or TeamCity).
- Experience investigating distributed systems, APIs, and service-to-service integrations using monitoring and logging tools.
What success looks like
Within your first few months, you’ll have a firm grasp of the DataGrip ecosystem and how its components interact across our IDEs. You’ll be independently identifying quality risks, setting clear testing priorities, and helping teams ship reliable releases without bottlenecks. Long-term, you’ll have established smoother QA workflows, making it easier for everyone to understand dependencies and catch cross-product issues before they reach our users.

Are you a hands-on engineer who loves zero-to-one challenges? Do you want to build systems with real context and memory that do more than reason, use tools, and drive actual business outcomes?
About JetBrains
We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. GrowthBricks is a shared business brain for GTM teams and AI agents.

Are you enthusiastic about shipping now, preferring to go live with rough ideas today over polishing presentations for next month? If so, this is the role for you.
In this role, you’ll join the team building Qure, an AI copilot for web testing automation. This desktop app turns manual testing flows into production-ready automated scripts, saving hours of manual coding. We’re a seven-person team funded directly by JetBrains.
About JetBrains Innovation Hub
JetBrains builds software development tools used by more than 15 million people, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100. Innovation Hub is its internal startup incubator, where small autonomous teams build new products, funded and employed by JetBrains. Qure runs inside the Innovation Hub with its own roadmap, go-to-market strategy, and customers.
For you, that means a founding role without the runway risk. You build acquisition from zero, with the funding, benefits, and stability of an established company behind you.
What you’ll do
Qure is a fresh product, so the acquisition channel map is practically blank. Paid search, video, newsletters, marketplaces, paid communities, and content are all unproven for Qure. We need someone to determine how best to find its audience. With a high degree of freedom, a lean team, and no marketing bureaucracy, decisions you make on Monday go live by Wednesday.
Day to day, you will:
- Run parallel channel experiments across paid search, video, communities, and organic traffic to discover what actually converts.
- Shut down underperforming channels early using your own data to ground the decision.
- Produce your own marketing assets, including ad copy, screen recordings, and landing pages.
- Work directly with the product team to ship acquisition-focused product requirements, such as custom onboarding flows or free tools.

jobs.title: Contract Senior Data Analyst (SQL,Telemetry,Browser Engine)
jobs.description:
The Gecko platform is the core engine of our product experience. To maintain competitiveness and user satisfaction, we must move beyond surface-level metrics to understand the deep correlations between engine performance and real-world user behavior. We currently face challenges with data quality, such as bot contamination in nightly telemetry, which obscures our understanding of true performance trends. A dedicated analyst is required to bridge the gap between engineering telemetry and actionable product strategy, ensuring that leadership has high-fidelity data to prioritize performance guardrails and technical budgets.
Engineering Deliverables
- Automated Dashboards: Create and maintain high-level overview dashboards that translate complex performance data into consumable formats for Product Managers and leadership.
- Telemetry Gap Analysis: Audit the Gecko codebase to identify missing collection points or "probes" necessary for a complete understanding of the product experience.
- Data Sanitization Frameworks: Develop methodologies and tools to identify and filter data inconsistencies, specifically focusing on isolating bot traffic and hardware-specific noise from telemetry streams.
- Behavioral Inference Reports: Deliver deep-dive analyses correlating technical performance shifts (e.g., LCP, eTLD+1) with user-facing pain points and engagement trends.
Scope, Skills, and Effort Estimate
Scope
The analyst will focus exclusively on Gecko engine telemetry across multiple platforms (Desktop and Android), collaborating with the Performance Team, Data Team, and Product Leadership.
Required Skills
- Technical: Advanced SQL (BigQuery/Redash), proficiency in data visualization using AI tooling, and experience with statistical analysis (e.g., Pearson’s correlation, multivariate analysis). Knowledge of Rust/C++ is a strong plus. Strong proficiency with AI tools like Claude Code, Codex, or similar is highly desirable.
- Domain Knowledge: Ability to understand browser component interactions and their impact on user experience.
- Soft Skills: Proven ability to work independently, translating technical requirements into business insights.
- Independent problem solving: Comfortable working in unfamiliar technical problem spaces and figuring out a path forward with minimal guidance, using documentation, experimentation, source code, data, and other available resources.
Hiring Ranges:
Remote UK
£58,500—£78,000 GBP

jobs.title: Senior Contract C++ / JavaScript Software Engineer (Browser Engine)
jobs.description:
The role
You will help the Firefox DOM Core team improve the health of the Session History area. You will write tests to improve the coverage; you will fix tests and/or problems to improve the Gecko correctness.
Responsibilities
- Write Web-Platform tests to improve the coverage, and Gecko mochitests as needed
- Fix the problems and pass the tests to improve the Gecko correctness
- Work through code review with the relevant Gecko module owners and iterate to landing
Definition of done
Improved Session History test coverage and code correctness in Gecko, measured by passed test cases, allowing the team’s senior engineers to focus on security, performance and strategic projects.
Required qualifications
- Substantial experience in a browser-engine codebase or in automating for a browser-engine, ideally Firefox/Gecko.
- Solid Javascript and applying that language skill to write automated tests.
- Proficiency in and experience developing software in C++.
- Strong debugging skills in a mature larget codebase.
- Comfort working in the open: public bugs, code review, and upstream landing.
Preferred
- Prior contributions to Gecko or another major browser engine.
- Familiarity with web standards and Web Platform Tests.

jobs.description:

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser, and Pocket, a service for keeping up with the best content online. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders - only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.
About this team and role:
We’re looking for a hands-on Mobile Product Manager with a primary focus on Firefox for iOS, while also contributing across mobile (including Android).
This role is about building a better browser, turning downloads into loyal users, and creating experiences that truly stand out. If you’ve shipped mobile apps, obsess over details that improve everyday use, and love turning user insights into real improvements, this is a great opportunity to drive impact at Firefox.
What you’ll do:
- Build a fundamentally better browser experience: fix bugs, refine UI and navigation, improve downloads, menus, performance, and all the small details that make Firefox noticeably better for users who care about privacy, quality and reliability.
- Drive strong activation and retention: focus on the new-user journey, quickly hooking people after they install the app, understanding where they drop off, and relentlessly optimizing the funnel through data, testing and iteration.
- Deliver differentiating features and experiences that make Firefox stickier for key user groups, the kinds of things others can’t or won’t build.
- Work closely with engineers, designers, data science and TPMs to ship high-impact improvements while balancing user needs, technical constraints, privacy and performance goals.
- Stay deeply connected to real users: track App Store trends and discussions, test apps hands-on, analyze reviews and analytics, and turn those insights into concrete enhancements for Firefox on iOS and Android.
- Monitor app health in App Store Connect and Google Play Console (crashes, ANRs, ratings) and support acquisition/retention efforts through ASO, store listings and growth experiments.
- Adapt and optimize Firefox for global markets (Europe, Japan, Asia etc.), keeping cultural differences and local realities like data constraints in mind.
What you'll bring:
- Proven Shipping Experience: Hands-on experience launching or managing apps on the iOS App Store and/or Google Play Store, with clear impact on user experience and metrics.
- Execution Focus: A strong track record of delivering features and improvements under deadlines through effective collaboration with engineering, design and cross-functional partners.
- Mobile & Browser Fluency: Deep understanding of iOS (and ideally Android) ecosystems, app store policies and web browser technologies, with genuine passion for what makes a great browsing experience.
- Data-Driven Iteration: Comfort using analytics, funnels, A/B testing and user feedback to improve activation, retention and overall product quality.
- User Obsession: Natural habit of studying apps, following trends on platforms like X/Twitter and Reddit, and testing experiences yourself to uncover opportunities.
- Global & Growth Mindset: Interest or experience growing products in international markets with sensitivity to local user needs.
- Bonus:
- Experience with mobile browsers or privacy-focused products.
- History of meaningfully scaling an app’s user base.
- Currently maintaining your own side project or app on the App Store or Google Play.
